key_insight: Detonation-sprayed Fe-based amorphous coatings with more circular, well-spread droplets form denser microstructures and show better long-term corrosion and humidity-dependent wear performance.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing spray parameters to minimize porosity can improve the durability of Fe-based amorphous protective coatings on carbon steel in corrosive and humid service environments.
method: Prepared Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 carbon steel by detonation spray under different spraying parameters.
Compared droplet morphology, coating microstructure, long-term corrosion behavior, and tribological performance under different humidity conditions.
Evaluated wear mechanisms involving Si3N4 balls and water-molecule-assisted tribo-chemical reactions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that droplets with the highest circularity and expansion factor produced fine-lamellar, dense coatings, while higher porosity correlated with reduced corrosion resistance and humidity increased corrosion and wear benefits.
watch_item: Performance appears sensitive to spray-parameter control and porosity formation, so process repeatability is critical before scale-up or field deployment.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
